subject: Commercial appendix: seat+token hybrid, rollover ledger & surge-sharing proposal
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara.park@novushealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com, tim.crawford@novushealth.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial appendix questions (seat/token hybrid)

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. We're reviewing the commercial appendix and have a few clarification requests before we complete our internal scoring:

1) You propose a "seat + token hybrid" model — we need a worked example comparing: a) 50 seats + 10M tokens/month committed vs b) 20 seats + 40M token commit. Show effective $/1000-token and overall monthly cap for both.

2) How do rollover credits work across quarters? Can excess unused pre-purchased tokens be carried for up to 2 quarters? If so, how are they consumed against overages?

3) You mention a "surge-sharing pool" in the appendix — what's the priority between burst pool consumption and per-route throttles? Any hard limits?

4) For embeddings you list a separate unit price — can embeddings credits be used for text-gen overage? If not, what is the reconciliation process if a customer reclassifies usage?

Attached is the commercial appendix we received with highlighted cells. Can we get a worked pricing model and a plain-English explanation we can share with procurement and finance?

Best,
Sara Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Novus Health

Attachment: Novus_RFP_Commercial_Appendix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial appendix questions (seat/token hybrid)

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear asks. Karthik and Marcus and I put together a short worked example and the commercial mechanics. Summary below, full model attached (Redwood_Token_Pricing_Model.csv).

High-level answers:
- Seat+Token worked example: we show the delta in blended $/1k tokens and also the fixed seat component amortized. Seats provide guaranteed concurrent throughput and lower per-token rates for steady-state generation; tokens give elasticity for spikes.

- Rollover credits: Unused pre-purchased token credits can be carried forward up to 2 fiscal quarters (i.e., the quarter they were purchased + 2 subsequent quarters) into a balance we call the "rollover ledger." Credits in the ledger are consumed before any paid overage and before burst-pool consumption. Ledger credits age out at the end of the 2nd quarter and are then expired.

- Surge-sharing pool: The surge pool is a paid burst buffer that customers can tap beyond committed tokens. Priority order for consumption: 1) Rollover ledger credits, 2) committed tokens, 3) surge-sharing pool (if configured), 4) on-demand overage rates. Route-level throttles apply concurrently — if a route is rate-limited, the pool will still be charged if requests are accepted by the platform but queued/limited per route. Max configurable pool size is 3x average committed token velocity; beyond that we fall back to on-demand rates.

- Embeddings vs text-gen crediting: Embeddings units are separate and do not automatically offset text-gen usage. We offer a one-time reclassification reconciliation: if during a contract year >10% of billed embeddings should have been text-gen, Redwood will convert embeddings credits to text-gen at a 1:1.6 token equivalence rate for reconciliation billing.

Attached model contains: per-scenario invoice line items, amortization schedule for seats, ledger math for rollover, and a sample invoice.

We can also convert the CSV into an anonymized PDF for procurement. If it helps, Marcus can step through the model on a 30-min call.

Thanks — Lukas
Head of Commercial Growth
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Token_Pricing_Model.csv (pricing model, 56KB)

Lukas — quick follow-up from finance: two items we need answered explicitly for our legal & accounting teams:

- Deferred billing / revenue recognition: if we buy seats upfront for 12 months, can seats be invoiced quarterly? We prefer quarterly invoicing tied to consumption thresholds. If Redwood requires annual prepay for seats, we need a clause to amortize credits monthly for ASC 606 purposes.

- Negative variance true-up: If actual usage in a month is materially below the committed token baseline, will Redwood credit back the difference, or simply carry forward to the rollover ledger? We need a mechanism to smooth budget impact.

Also — Marcus, are there any standard clauses you can share that describe the ledger mechanics for auditors?

Thanks,
Tim
VP Finance, Novus Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Crawford <tim.crawford@novushealth.com>, Sara Park <sara.park@novushealth.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial appendix questions (seat/token hybrid)

Tim — good questions. A few concise points for legal/accounting that we can include in contract language: 

1) Invoicing / revenue recognition: Seats can be invoiced on a quarterly schedule (billing at t0, t+3m, etc.) with a purchased-seat credit ledger created at invoice time. For ASC 606 alignment we will provide a monthly amortization schedule reflecting the consumed portion of the seat invoice; the ledger balance will appear as a prepaid asset on Redwood's books and as a usage credit on the customer's side.

2) Negative variance true-up (smoothing): By default unused committed tokens are carried into the rollover ledger (see Lukas' note). For customers requesting budget smoothing we offer an optional monthly "negative variance credit" (NVC) program: if monthly usage < 70% of committed baseline, Redwood will issue an invoice credit equal to 50% of the shortfall (shortfall measured in tokens converted to $ at the committed per-token rate). The remaining 50% is carried to the rollover ledger. NVC is mutually agreed at contract signing.

3) Audit language / ledger description (recommended clause):
- "Rollover Ledger: Unused committed token credits will be recorded in a customer-specific ledger and may be applied to subsequent consumption for up to two (2) fiscal quarters from the month of purchase. Credits are consumed prior to overage charges and will be visually surfaced in monthly usage exports. Expired credits will be listed on the final quarter statement."

We can provide a sample invoice and a csv export schema for auditors. Lukas — should we offer the NVC as part of the initial term or make it an add-on? If the customer is sensitive to budget smoothing, offering it as an optional add-on with a modest fee is our preference (reduces revenue unpredictability for Redwood).

— Marcus
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Commercial appendix questions (seat/token hybrid)

Sara / Tim — attaching a one-page summary for procurement and the final CSV model. Key takeaways in plain English:

- Two example scenarios provided: 50 seats + 10M tokens vs 20 seats + 40M tokens. Blended $/1k tokens differs by ~22% in favor of higher seat counts at steady-state, but seats carry fixed cost risk.

- Rollover ledger: credits are consumed first; they expire after two quarters. Ledger consumption precedence reduces near-term overage exposure.

- Surge-sharing pool: configurable up to 3x committed velocity; charges at a pre-negotiated surge rate (midway between committed and on-demand). Route throttles still apply.

- Negative variance credit (optional add-on): will credit 50% of any monthly shortfall <70% of baseline; the remaining 50% moves to the ledger. This is designed for predictable budgeting and is chargeable as a small % of committed volume.

Next steps:
- If this matches Novus' needs, we'll: 1) mark NVC as an add-on on the term sheet, 2) insert the ledger clause into SOW/contract, and 3) schedule a 30-min pricing walkthrough (Marcus + Karthik + Lukas).

I'll send the one-pager and the model now.

Regards,
Lukas
